## Metapsy (psychotherapy)

Studies included in _Metapsy_ (<https://www.metapsy.org/>), a set of living meta-analytic databases of randomised trials of psychotherapeutic interventions.

**Snapshot date:**
January 2026

**Data availability:**
Metapsy is maintained by an international collaboration led by Vrije Universiteit 
Amsterdam. Databases are available at <https://www.metapsy.org/> and through the 
R package `metapsyData` [@harrer2022metapsydata]. The Metapsy FAQ states that all 
data provided as part of the project are open access and that attribution is required.
The source contains RCTs of psychotherapeutic interventions.

**Data processing:**
We merged 20 individual datasets in Metapsy and performed some cleaning (e.g. to extract
study dates from titles). Almost all estimates are Hedges' g, but for one of
the databases (`total-response`) we converted log-odds ratios to SMD (dividing
by $\Pi/\sqrt{3}$ to scale SD of logistic regression) to keep a comparable scale. 
Signed z-values were computed as effect sizes divided by their standard errors.


**Study characteristics:**

- **Sample size and year:** `ss` is the sum of `n_arm1` and `n_arm2` when both are supplied; `year` is the source year or a year parsed from the study label.

- **Study ID:** we use the source `study` label within each database.
- **Meta-analysis ID:** we use the Metapsy database identifier.
- **Topic:** we use an explicit clinical-subject lookup; 
  datasets `peer-support` and `total-response` are labelled as "mental health".
- Effects are standardised mean differences, mainly Hedges' g; a minority are 
  converted from log odds ratios.
